messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: High 502/504 rate from inference-api in az1a. 10m rolling errors 18% (svc: inference-hosting). See /alerts/alerts1234

Nadia L: I'm on it, grabbing the oncall console. quick check - is this limited to az1a?

Sam K: Confirmed from dashboards — errors spike only for az1a backend pool. az1b/az1c look normal. CPU/GPU usage on nodes is fine.

Jonah P: I'm seeing a lot of TCP conn resets and half-open sockets in the pod logs. Could be SNAT exhaustion on the NAT instance/gateway.

Maria G: Can we check natgateway/elb metrics? 502s + connection failures often align with ephemeral port exhaustion.

Nadia L: Running quick CW query: `aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/NATGateway --metric-name PacketsIn --start-time ...` but console shows high `ActiveConnections` nearing the port limit on the az1a NAT gateway.

Sam K: Run `curl -s http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/local-ipv4` on a proxy pod and then `ss -s` to see established connections. Also check `conntrack -L | wc -l` on the NAT host.

Jonah P: Pasted results:
```
# on proxy-01 (az1a)
$ ss -s
TCP:   established: 1500  orphaned: 0  timewait: 24000
$ conntrack -L | wc -l
> 65500
```
Suggests we're hitting conntrack/port limits.

Maria G: Ok that's consistent. Likely SNAT port pool exhausted -> new outbound connections fail -> proxies return 502. Any recent traffic pattern changes? Optimize batching?

Sam K: Noted a traffic spike from a particular customer `video-captioning` running large batch jobs this morning. They opened a large concurrent stream of short requests. That plus retries may have burned ports.

Nadia L: Immediate mitigations: 1) Temporarily enable proxy-level outbound connection reuse / connection pooling; 2) Reduce client concurrency via rate-limit rule for that customer; 3) Redispatch egress via az1b NATs.

Jonah P: I can flip low-risk traffic steering: update route policy to prefer az1b for new sessions and leave az1a for sticky sessions. Command (netknife): `netknife steer --scope inference-egress --from az1a --to az1b --weight 75`

deploy-bot: runbook step executed: updated route policy, draining 20% from az1a -> az1b.

Maria G: Also increasing conntrack table size and ephemeral port range on NAT hosts as temporary relief. On NAT hosts: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000` and `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range=\"1024 65535\"`.

Sam K: Applying the conntrack bump now on az1a NATs. Will monitor.

Nadia L: Notifying customers: posting to customer-bulletin for affected beta users; internal comms to CS to prepare for support tickets. Estimated impact window 30-45m.

Jonah P: After steering + conntrack increase: 5 minutes metrics: errors down from 18% -> 7%, tail latencies improved 2x. Still some error tail at 1-2%.

Maria G: Rolling a config change to proxy to prefer keepalive (reduce outbound churn). Patch pushed to canary group in az1a.

Sam K: Handing pager to Maria G in 20m — must be ready to expand steering to az1c if we see more burn. Adding escalation to infra lead if error >5% for 15m.

Maria G: Acked, taking over. I'll keep monitoring and coordinate with infra.

Nadia L: Action items summary:
- Maria: monitor error rate & finish keepalive rollout (owner)
- Sam: liaise with customer `video-captioning` to throttle concurrency (owner)
- Jonah: track conntrack counts + cleanup scripts (owner)
- Nadia: customer comms + post-incident blameless summary repo entry

Sam K: Quick snippet to check metrics: `curl \"https://grafana/api/ds/query\" -d '{...query for 502s by az...}'`

Maria G: 30m after mitigation - errors at 0.6% in az1a, latency normalized. Moving to monitoring state; keeping steering in place for 2 hours to allow traffic rebalancing.

incident-bot: Incident resolved -> severity: SEV3 (service degradation); start: 3410012345, end: 3410012700. Please file a postmortem.

Nadia L: Will open the postmortem and include runbook changes: detect SNAT port exhaustion earlier, automate proactive steering, add quota guardrails per-tenant, and add elastic NAT failover playbook.

Sam K: Thx team. Follow-ups: add telemetry alert for conntrack utilization + per-tenant ephemeral port use.

Maria G: handing back to Nadia now. Good job team :thumbsup:
